hub.meta_title: Letting agents in Swansea | Hello New Home
hub.meta_description: Swansea letting agents licensed by Rent Smart Wales. Full management 12%, capped at £150 a month, no VAT, no lock-in. Long lets, shared houses, short lets.
hub.intro: Hello New Home started in Swansea and runs every area from the office on Central Business Park, SA7. We manage long lets, shared houses through hellomyroom and short lets across SA1 to SA18, from the Marina to Mumbles and from Morriston to Llanelli. Full management is 12% of the rent, capped at £150 a month, with no VAT added and no lock-in. We are licensed by Rent Smart Wales, and the people who answer the phone live here.

sections.h2: Why Swansea landlords move to us
sections.html:
Most landlords who call us are paying a percentage plus extras to a high-street agent, tied in for 12 months, and have had a letter from Rent Smart Wales they did not understand. The rest are self-managing and chasing a late rent for the third month running.

The fee is 12% of the rent and stops at £150 a month however high the rent goes. Nothing is added for VAT. You can leave with 30 days' notice and no exit fee. And the Welsh paperwork is done by people who do it every day, from an office you can drive to.

Rent Smart Wales issued 3,198 fixed penalties in the year to May 2026, almost all for landlords who were not registered or licensed. The fix is a form and a course, and we tell you which.

sections.h2: Swansea rents and what the cap means for you
sections.html:
The ONS average private rent for Swansea was £838 a month in May 2026, up 5.5% on the year from £794, against 4.7% across Wales. At that rent our fee is about £101 a month.

The cap starts to matter at £1,250 a month. A three or four-bed in Sketty, Killay or Mumbles can let above that, and at £1,400 a percentage-only agent would take £168 while we take £150. The further rents rise, the wider that gap gets.

An average is not your rent. Your free rent review uses what is actually letting on your street this month.

sections.h2: Licensing and the Welsh rules, handled
sections.html:
Every landlord in Wales must be registered with Rent Smart Wales and either licensed or using a licensed agent. We are the licensed agent, and we check your registration when you join.

Under the Renting Homes (Wales) Act 2016 your tenant is a contract-holder (that is what Wales calls a tenant) and the agreement is an occupation contract. The contract-holder must have a written statement within 14 days of moving in. A no-fault notice under section 173 needs six months' notice and cannot be served in the first six months. Holding deposits are capped at one week's rent. We draft, serve and diarise all of it.

Mandatory licensing covers larger HMOs across the city, and from 14 February 2026 additional licensing covers every HMO in Castle, Uplands, St Thomas and Waterfront wards for five years. If your Brynmill house is let by the room, that is hellomyroom, our shared-house team, and they manage the licence and the fire safety with it.

sections.h2: The streets and who rents them
sections.html:
Swansea is several rental markets in one postcode area.

  • SA1 and the Marina: professionals on long lets, and short stays driven by the Arena and the waterfront.
  • Uplands and Brynmill: shared houses for students; Swansea University, UWTSD and Gower College together support almost 30,000 full-time students.
  • Sketty and Killay: families and staff from Singleton Hospital, where rents reach the cap.
  • Morriston and Llansamlet: hospital staff, DVLA employees and families, on steady long lets.
  • Mumbles and Gower: holiday lets in summer, and a 100% council tax premium on second homes that miss the business-rates test.
  • Neath, Port Talbot and Llanelli: long lets at rents where 12% is a modest fee.

Swansea had 108,000 employees in 2023, 30.4% in the public sector, so demand for ordinary long lets near the hospitals and the university does not swing with the season.

sections.h2: Long let, shared house or short let: one team runs all three
sections.html:
A high-street agent will not run your Marina flat as a short let, and a national co-host will not take it back as a long let when bookings thin out in November. We do both, from the same office, so the decision is maths rather than habit.

Flex Switch is included with every managed property: it can move between a long let, a shared house and a short let with us, with no re-onboarding. A Gower cottage can be a holiday let from April to September and a winter let after. A Sketty house that should stay a family let stays one.

Start with a free rent review. Give us the address and we call within one working day with an honest rent figure, your Rent Smart Wales position and a written fee comparison against what you pay now. If you think the property might earn more as a short let, ask for the free short-let appraisal instead and we run both sets of numbers side by side. The Swansea team will come to you if you prefer.

faqs.q: Are you licensed by Rent Smart Wales?
faqs.a: Yes. Hello New Home is a Rent Smart Wales licensed agent, and the licence number is shown on our fees page. Every landlord in Wales must also be registered with Rent Smart Wales, which we check when you join us and help you complete if it is missing.

faqs.q: How much does full management cost in Swansea?
faqs.a: Full management is 12% of the monthly rent, capped at £150 a month. No VAT is added. On the Swansea average rent of £838 that is about £101 a month. Tenant Find on its own is £495, no let no fee.

faqs.q: Do I need an HMO licence in Swansea?
faqs.a: Larger shared houses need a mandatory licence anywhere in the city. From 14 February 2026, every HMO in Castle, Uplands, St Thomas and Waterfront wards needs an additional licence. Our shared-house team, hellomyroom, checks your address and manages the application.

It is the Welsh name for a tenancy agreement under the Renting Homes (Wales) Act 2016. The tenant is called a contract-holder and must receive a written statement of the contract within 14 days of moving in. We prepare and serve it as part of management.

faqs.q: Can I leave if I am not happy?
faqs.a: Yes. There is no lock-in on any of our services. You can end full management with 30 days' notice and there is no exit fee. Your contract-holder stays in place, and we hand the file over cleanly to you or your next agent.

sections.h2: The Welsh paperwork we do for you
sections.html:
Since 1 December 2022 every let in Wales runs under the Renting Homes (Wales) Act 2016. Your tenant is a contract-holder and the agreement is an occupation contract. We issue the written occupation contract, give the written statement within 14 days and keep a signed copy on file.

Rent rises go on form RHW12 with at least two months' notice and no more than once a year. A section 173 no-fault notice needs six months and cannot be served in the first six months of the contract; if you need the property back, we tell you the earliest honest date rather than the one you were hoping for.

The property side is on the same calendar: an annual gas safety check, an electrical report every five years, mains-powered interlinked smoke alarms on every storey and a carbon monoxide alarm wherever there is a gas, oil or solid-fuel appliance. The EPC must be band E now and band C by 1 October 2030, and we flag the work needed well before then.

sections.h2: Moving a tenanted property to us
sections.html:
If your property in Uplands or Morriston is already let through another agent, you do not have to wait for the contract-holder to leave. We serve your notice on the current agent, collect the deposit and the file, check the occupation contract and certificates against the Act, and introduce ourselves to the contract-holder in person. For them, the only thing that changes is the repairs number.

If anything in the file is missing, a written statement that was never served or an EICR that is out of date, we tell you first and fix it second. We do not describe a property as compliant until we have inspected it.

sections.h2: Your next step: a free rent review
sections.html: Request a free rent review with the address and your current fee. Within one working day the Swansea team calls back with a realistic rent based on current lets on your street, your Rent Smart Wales position, and a written comparison of what you pay now against 12% capped at £150. There is no obligation and nobody from the office will keep ringing.

faqs.q: What does 12% capped at £150 a month actually mean?
faqs.a: You pay 12% of each month's rent until that reaches £150, and never more than £150. On an £838 rent the fee is about £101. On a £1,500 rent it is £150. There is no VAT added to any Hello New Home fee.

faqs.q: Do you handle Rent Smart Wales for me?
faqs.a: We are the licensed agent, so you do not need your own licence while we manage the property. You still need to be registered as a landlord with Rent Smart Wales, and we check that at onboarding and help you complete it if it is missing.

faqs.q: How much notice does a contract-holder get in Wales?
faqs.a: A section 173 no-fault notice needs at least six months and cannot be given in the first six months of the occupation contract. Where there is a breach, such as serious rent arrears, shorter notice routes apply. We advise on the right notice for your situation.

faqs.q: Can you take over a property that is already let?
faqs.a: Yes. We give notice to your current agent, transfer the deposit and file, check the paperwork against the Renting Homes Act and meet the contract-holder in person. The contract-holder stays, and the only change for them is the repairs number.

shortlets.meta_title: Airbnb & short-let management Swansea | Hello New Home
shortlets.meta_description: Short-let management in Swansea, Mumbles and Gower. 18% of net booking revenue, Welsh rules handled, and a free appraisal against a long let first.
shortlets.h1: Airbnb and short-let management in Swansea
shortlets.intro: Some Swansea flats earn more as short lets. Some do not. We run long lets and short lets from the same office, so our free appraisal shows your property both ways, net of platform fees, cleaning, utilities and management, before you decide. If the short let wins, Full SA Management is 18% of net booking revenue and we handle pricing, guests, cleaning and the Welsh rules. If the long let wins, we say so and manage that instead.

sections.h2: Where short stays work in Swansea, and where they do not
sections.html:
Short-stay demand here has three engines: the Arena and the waterfront for SA1 and the Marina, Gower and Mumbles for summer and bank-holiday weeks, and the university and the two hospitals for stays of a few nights to a few weeks. The city has no 12-month season, and we price for the one it has.

A two-bed in SA1 with a Marina view, five minutes from the Arena, can book well through spring, summer and event weekends and should expect a quieter January. A Mumbles or Gower cottage fills from Easter to September and may do better as a winter let after that. A student-area house in Brynmill is usually worth more as a long let or a shared house, and we say so rather than list it.

sections.h2: What we charge and what you keep
sections.html:
• Full SA Management, 18% of net booking revenue: dynamic pricing, guest vetting and messaging 24 hours a day, cleaning and linen coordination, restocking, maintenance, reviews, a monthly owner statement and the 182-day tracker. Cleaning is passed through at cost.
  • SA Co-Host, 12%: pricing, guest communication and the listing only; you run the cleaning. For owners who only want the hard part taken away.
  • SA Launch, £495: photography, Airbnb, Booking.com and direct-booking listings, pricing rules, house manual, smart-lock and noise-monitor advice, and the compliance pack. Waived with 12 months of Full SA Management.

No VAT is added to any of it, and there is no 12-month minimum: 30 days' notice, no exit fee.

sections.h2: The Welsh rules for a short let, in plain words
sections.html:
Wales treats short lets differently from England, and the appraisal puts the position for your address in writing.

Planning. Since 20 October 2022 a short-term let is its own use class, C6. Councils can remove the right to switch a home into C6 by an Article 4 direction. We have found no such direction in Swansea, and we check again before every launch.

Business rates or council tax. A Welsh holiday let is only rated as a business if it is available for 252 days and actually let for 182 days a year. Miss that and it pays council tax, and Swansea charges a 100% premium on second homes, with most of them in Gower, Swansea West and the Marina. Our 182-day tracker tells you where you stand every month.

The register. The Welsh visitor accommodation register opened on 1 October 2026. Existing providers must register by 31 March 2027 and registration is free. We do it as part of SA Launch.

Safety. A fire risk assessment, gas and electrical certificates, PAT testing and an insurance check sit in the compliance pack. It is the checklist we work to, not legal advice.

sections.h2: Flex Switch: when the numbers change, the property moves
sections.html: A Gower cottage might be a holiday let from April to September and a six-month winter let after. A Marina flat might run as a short let until a contract-holder appears at the right rent. With us it is the same agent, the same statement and no re-onboarding either way. A co-host working from a laptop in another city cannot offer that; a high-street agent will not touch the short-let half.

sections.h2: Your next step: a free short-let appraisal
sections.html: Ask for the free short-let appraisal and tell us the address. You get two columns, long let and short let, net of every cost and using Swansea occupancy rather than a national average, plus the planning, 182-day and register position for your property in writing. If you would rather start with the long-let figure alone, the free rent review gives you that within one working day.

faqs.q: How much does short-let management cost in Swansea?
faqs.a: Full SA Management is 18% of net booking revenue, with cleaning passed through at cost. SA Co-Host, where you run the cleaning, is 12%. SA Launch is £495 and is waived with 12 months of Full SA Management. No VAT is added and there is no 12-month minimum.

faqs.q: Do I need planning permission for a short let in Swansea?
faqs.a: Short-term lets in Wales have had their own use class, C6, since 20 October 2022. A council can stop homes switching to C6 with an Article 4 direction. We have found none in Swansea, we check before each launch, and the appraisal states the position for your address.

A Welsh holiday let pays business rates only if it is available for 252 days and actually let for 182 days a year. Otherwise it pays council tax, and Swansea adds a 100% premium on second homes. Our tracker reports your night count every month.

faqs.q: Do I have to register my holiday let in Wales?
faqs.a: Yes. The Welsh visitor accommodation register opened on 1 October 2026. Existing providers must register by 31 March 2027, and registration is free. We complete it as part of SA Launch.

faqs.q: Will a short let always earn more than a long let?
faqs.a: No. A Marina flat near the Arena often does; a house in Brynmill or Morriston usually does not. The free appraisal shows both figures net of every cost, and if the long let wins we manage that instead.
